messages.subject: Re: Italicize alternate names with geom_tiplab
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Is there a way of getting this 2017 example to work with fontface? I haven't found a way of applying a different fontface to 'label' and to 'alternate_names'.

All I can get is having the two labels overlapping one another depending on separate geom_tiplab:

p1 + geom_tiplab(align=FALSE , linesize=0, aes(label=label),fontface = 3)+ geom_tiplab(aes(label=alternate_names),fontface = 1)

Thanks.

On Monday, July 17, 2017 at 12:51:22 AM UTC-7 gc...@connect.hku.hk wrote:

> treeplot +
>     geom_tiplab(aes(label=paste0('italic(', label, ')~italic(', alternate_names, ')')),
>                 parse=TRUE)
>
> On Fri, Jul 14, 2017 at 11:07 PM, <bena...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > Here is a reproducible example. The example you linked to is for a single node, and if I try and copy the syntax it doesn't work for applying to all the tip labels.
> >
> >
> > library(ggtree)
> > tree <- rtree(5)
> > alternate_names <- c("a","b","c","d","e")
> > name_frame <- data.frame(cbind(tree$tip.label,alternate_names))
> > treeplot <- ggtree(tree) %<+% name_frame
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label=label))                                                                            #this works
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label=alternate_names))                                                         #this works
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label=paste(label,alternate_names)))                                      #this works
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label=italic(label)))                                                                   #does not work
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label='italic(label)'), parse=TRUE)                                           #prints italic, but does not reference the label
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label='italic(alternate_names)'), parse=TRUE)                        #same as above
> > treeplot + geom_tiplab(aes(label='paste(italic(label),altername_names)'), parse=TRUE)  #this is the desired function, but does not work

> > > > ggtree(tree) %<+% names_frame + geom_tiplab(aes(label=aligned))
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > But how do I make it italic? If I try the following using the format of https://guangchuangyu.github.io/ggtree/faq/#inherit-aes it does not. I think it is because it cannot read aligned as a object since it is inside quotes, but I do not know how to get around that.

messages.subject: Beast trees and mrsd scale
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

How is the time scale calculated using the mrsd argument?

There seems to be quite major dependencies between node heights (BEAST2) and node x-axis coordinate dates (ggtree) after mrsd is passed.

When doing the calculation manually (with lubridate) using the Beast node height estimate subtracted from the mrsd (or calculating with as.duration), the result does not equal the ggtree scale coordinate. This particularly becomes a problem when working with the 95% HPD range (e.g., manually plotting just one HPD interval accurately).

I am wondering if there could be a way to apply a correction so dates from node heights and ggtree mrsd x-axis dates are the same?

Many thanks,
Chris

messages.subject: Points on edges
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm working with output from the Evolutionary Placement Algorithm (https://cme.h-its.org/exelixis/web/software/epa/index.html). This algorithm allows a user to "place" a set of reads onto a reference tree resulting in a list of "placements" along edges of a phylogenetic tree. Each placement has a mapping to which particular edge it has been placed along with a distance from the ancestral node for placement. I'm wondering if geom_point() has been extended to edges so that perhaps I could call geom_point() with a list of edges and distance from ancestor node along that edge. Then points could be put along the edges of the tree rather than solely at the nodes.

+Holly

messages.subject: Re: Points on edges
messages.body_plain:
Hi Holly,

That's very doable. First plot your tree, extract the data, find your node's x-y coordinates, then plot a custom geom_point() using the node's (adjusted x) coordinates. As such:

tree <- ggtree(phy)
tree.dat <- tree$data
tree.dat[tree.dat$node[<node number>], c("x", "y")] # prints node of interest coords
tree + geom_point(data=data.frame(x=<adjusted node x>, y=<node y>), aes(x=x, y=y) # use above coords with adjusted x to move point along edge

Cheers,
Chris
